title: Social force model for pedestrian dynamics
method_family: social force model; nonlinearly coupled Langevin equations; potential fields
human_is: self-driven particle subject to social forces
social_repr: repulsive elliptical potentials (personal space/territory), border repulsion, attraction to persons/objects, anisotropic perception
math_model: dw/dt = F_driving + sum F_repulsive(peds) + sum F_border + sum F_attractive + fluctuations; speed capped at v_max = 1.3 v0
planner: None (descriptive pedestrian model); later used as robot controller/planner
strengths: Simple, interpretable, reproduces lane formation and doorway oscillation
limitations: Hand-tuned parameters; no intention/context; reactive; groups only via attraction
later_improvement: Extended SFM for robots and groups (Moussaid 2010; Ferrer); used in simulators (PedSim, HuNavSim) and as demonstrator (GAIL-Depth); learned and VLM-based methods target context and norms it lacks

title: Unfreezing the Robot: Navigation in Dense, Interacting Crowds
method_family: Gaussian processes; interaction potential; importance sampling / particle inference; MAP joint trajectory planning; receding horizon
human_is: interacting stochastic agent whose trajectory is a GP coupled to others
social_repr: joint collision avoidance via multiplicative interaction potential among all agents including robot
hand_rules: Partial (potential form and h, alpha hand-set)
math_model: p_IGP(f_R, f | z) = (1/Z) psi(f_R, f) prod_i p(f_i | z); MAP via importance sampling
strengths: Formalizes freezing robot problem; models cooperation; goals as GP measurements; handles multimodality via sampling
limitations: Assumes cooperative humans; computational cost grows with particles; offline replay validation
later_improvement: IJRR 2015 real-robot cafeteria study; DRL methods (CADRL/SARL) learn cooperation implicitly; VLM approaches add semantic context

title: Feature-Based Prediction of Trajectories for Socially Compliant Navigation
method_family: maximum entropy IRL (continuous); spline trajectory optimization (RPROP); topological variants (homotopy classes); joint human-robot trajectory prediction
social_repr: learned cost over trajectory features + passing-side topology
math_model: p_theta(x) = exp(-theta^T f(x)) / Z(theta); modes approximated per topological variant
planner: robot plans its own trajectory as part of most likely joint trajectory
strengths: Models cooperation and passing decisions probabilistically; human-like smooth trajectories
limitations: Small data; requires known goals; computational growth with agents (variants grow combinatorially)
later_improvement: Kretzschmar IJRR 2016 (larger study, robot experiments); later DRL and VLM methods

title: Socially Compliant Mobile Robot Navigation via Inverse Reinforcement Learning
method_family: maximum entropy IRL; Hybrid (Hamiltonian) Monte Carlo; homotopy classes via Voronoi graph; spline trajectory optimization (RPROP); shared autonomy
social_repr: learned costs over trajectory dynamics and topological decisions
math_model: p(x) = P(psi_x) p_psi(x); p_psi(x) ∝ exp(-theta^T f(x)); P(psi) ∝ exp(-theta_hom^T f_hom(psi))
planner: most likely composite trajectory in most likely homotopy class; Voronoi-based homotopy enumeration; global A* beyond horizon
strengths: Captures discrete and continuous decisions and stochasticity; learns cultural side preferences and group avoidance in principle; teachable by teleoperation
limitations: Assumes cooperative agents and known goals; small datasets; computational complexity with many agents
later_improvement: DRL (SA-CADRL) and VLM methods; SCAND-based learning

title: Learning Socially Normative Robot Navigation Behaviors with Bayesian Inverse Reinforcement Learning
method_family: inverse reinforcement learning (Bayesian, trajectory-based TBIRL); controller graph (SMDP); costmap-based planning (A* + elastic band)
human_is: agent with personal spaces and social ties
social_repr: learned costmap over proxemic and relation features
math_model: MDP/SMDP on controller graph; Bayesian IRL posterior (Eq.5-9)
planner: weighted A* on learned costmap + elastic band
strengths: Context-dependent behaviours (polite/sociable/rude) from few demonstrations; groups respected
limitations: Feature engineering; behaviours defined by demonstrator; proxy social metrics
later_improvement: DRL and VLM methods generalize context and norms without hand-crafted features
